fullText:
Disney invoked 9 U.S.C. § 3 to seek a court pause in Jeffrey Piccolo’s wrongful-death lawsuit while pushing his claims against Disney into arbitration.

The asserted consent chain ran from a one-month Disney+ trial in 2019 to ticket-purchasing account terms accepted in September 2023—and then to a restaurant-death claim.​ Disney also argued that an arbitrator should decide the agreement’s reach, citing language granting “exclusive authority” over interpretation, applicability and enforceability. This was a contested argument for arbitration and a stay—not a judicially established release from liability.​

The receipt: Orange County, Florida, Case No. 2024-CA-001616-O; Disney’s Motion to Compel Arbitration and Stay Case, May 31, 2024, citing Terms of Use Section 7, “Binding Arbitration and Class Action Waiver.” Disney withdrew the motion on August 20, 2024, allowing the case to proceed in court.

Before accepting linked account terms, save the dated agreement and follow every incorporated document. Check which affiliates and products it covers—and whether an arbitrator gets authority to decide that coverage. Those were the contractual links Disney invoked.
